rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse concerns the hypocrites.
rows.anchor: أنزلت هذه الآية في ذكر المنافقين.

rows.speaker: محمد بن السميقع اليماني
rows.claim: He reads لاقوا; its underlying form is لاقيوا, with the vowel change and deletion caused by two adjoining quiescent letters.
rows.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن السميقع اليماني: «لاقوا الذين آمنوا».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw remains in لاقوا because a fatḥa precedes it, while it is dropped in لقوا because a preceding ḍamma makes another ḍamma heavy on the tongue.
rows.anchor: لثقلها، وحركت في لاقوا لأن قبلها فتحة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here خلوا means they went away or departed, which explains its construction with إلى; al-Farazdaq's use of صرف supports this sense.
rows.anchor: «خلوا» هنا بمعنى ذهبوا وانصرفوا ومنه قول الفرزدق:

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some interpret إلى as مع, though al-Qurṭubī considers this weak.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: «إلى» بمعنى مع وفيه ضعف.

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take إلى to mean باء, but al-Khalil and Sibawayh reject that interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: «إلى» بمعنى الباء وهذا يأباه الخليل وسيبويه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes إلى literally: they withdrew from the believers to their devils.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى وإذا خلوا من المؤمنين إلى شياطينهم ف «إلى» على بابها.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: They identify the devils as the leaders of disbelief.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس والسدي: هم رؤساء الكفر.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He identifies the devils as jinn.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هم شياطين الجن.

rows.speaker: جمع من المفسرين
rows.claim: A group of commentators identify them as soothsayers.
rows.anchor: وقال جمع من المفسرين: هم الكهان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word's sense of distance from faith and good encompasses all the groups named.
rows.anchor: ولفظ الشيطنة الذي معناه البعد عن الإيمان والخير يعم جميع من ذكر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مستهزئون means they deny what they are summoned to believe.
rows.anchor: أي مكذبون بما ندعى إليه.

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they are mocking or scoffing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ساخرون. والهزء: السخرية واللعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root هزء denotes mockery and play; the rajaz line illustrates هزئت.
rows.anchor: والهزء: السخرية واللعب يقال: هزىء به واستهزأ قال الراجز:

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: A further etymology makes استهزاء mean taking vengeance, illustrated by a line from another poet.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أصل الاستهزاء: الانتقام كما قال الآخر:

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: The waw in اشتروا takes ḍamma to distinguish it from an original waw, as in a verse from Sūrat al-Jinn.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه: ضمت الواو في «اشتروا» فرقا بينها وبين الواو الأصلية

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: He says ḍamma is lightest on waw because the vowel is of its own kind.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: الضمة في الواو أخف من غيرها لأنها من جنسها.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He explains the waw's ḍamma by analogy with نحن.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: حركت بالضم كما فعل في «نحن».

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحق ويحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: They read the waw with kasra, following the original rule for two adjoining quiescent letters.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحق ويحيى بن يعمر بكسر الواو على أصل التقاء الساكنين.

rows.speaker: أبو زيد الأنصاري عن قعنب أبي السمال العدوي
rows.claim: He transmits a fatḥa reading, chosen for lightness even though the preceding letter is fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو زيد الأنصاري عن قعنب أبي السمال العدوي أنه قرأ بفتح الواو

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: He permits hamza on the waw with ḍamma, like أدؤر.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الكسائي همز الواو وضمها كأدؤر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buying is metaphorical: they preferred disbelief to faith, since a buyer chooses what he wants; this is not an actual sale of faith they had possessed.
rows.anchor: والشراء هنا مستعار. والمعنى استحبوا الكفر على الإيمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses the exchange as taking misguidance and abandoning guidance, that is, choosing disbelief over faith.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أخذوا الضلالة وتركوا الهدى. ومعناه استبدلوا واختاروا الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purchase wording is an expansive metaphor because Arabs use buying and trade for any substitution; the cited line describes trading forbearance for ignorance.
rows.anchor: لأن الشراء والتجارة راجعان إلى الاستبدال والعرب تستعمل ذلك في كل من استبدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضلالة primarily means bewilderment; forgetting is called misguidance because it involves confusion.
rows.anchor: وأصل الضلالة: الحيرة. ويسمى النسيان ضلالة لما فيه من الحيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguidance can also mean destruction, as in the question about being lost in the earth.
rows.anchor:
ويسمى الهلاك ضلالة كما قال عز وجل:
وقالوا أإذا ضللنا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing profit to the trade follows Arabic idiom; the intended meaning is that the traders themselves made no profit.
rows.anchor: أسند تعالى الربح إلى التجارة على عادة العرب في قولهم: ربح بيعك، وخسرت صفقتك

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: He allows the plurals تجائر for تجارة and ضلائل for ضلالة.
rows.anchor: ابن كيسان: ويجوز تجارة وتجائر، وضلالة وضلائل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were not guided in choosing misguidance.
rows.anchor: وما كانوا مهتدين } في اشترائهم الضلالة.

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Another explanation is that their lack of guidance was already present in God's prior knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في سابق علم الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذين may be accusative as an adjective for الفاسقين, or nominative as the predicate of an omitted هو.
rows.anchor: «الذين» في موضع نصب على النعت للفاسقين، وإن شئت جعلته في موضع رفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نقض is undoing what one has firmly bound, such as a structure, rope, or covenant; the passage also notes related forms for unraveling, contradiction, and counter-poetry.
rows.anchor: النقض: إفساد ما أبرمته من بناء أو حبل أو عهد.

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: One view identifies the covenant as the pledge God took from Adam's descendants when He brought them from his back.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هو الذي أخذه الله على بني آدم حين استخرجهم من ظهره.

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Another view makes the covenant God's commands and prohibitions delivered through His books and messengers; breaking it means failing to act on them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو وصية الله تعالى إلى خلقه، وأمره إياهم بما أمرهم به

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Another view treats the signs of God's oneness in the heavens, earth, and creation as a covenant, broken by neglecting to reflect on them.
rows.anchor: بل نصب الأدلة على وحدانيته بالسموات والأرض وسائر الصنعة هو بمنزلة العهد

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Another view concerns scriptural communities commanded to disclose Muhammad's prophethood rather than conceal it.
rows.anchor: هو ما عهده إلى من أوتي الكتاب أن يبينوا نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا يكتموا أمره.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He says the covenant God took from prophets and their followers was not to disbelieve in the Prophet, citing the covenant passage in Āl ʿImrān.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق الزجاج: عهده جل وعز ما أخذه على النبيين ومن اتبعهم ألا يكفروا بالنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the preceding and following context appears to concern unbelievers, he says the second, general account of God's commands gathers the other views.
rows.anchor: قلت: وظاهر ما قبل وما بعد يدل على أنها في الكفار. فهذه خمسة أقوال والقول الثاني يجمعها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ميثاق is a strongly confirmed covenant, from الوثاقة and the firmness of binding; its plurals include مواثيق and dialectal variants, supported by a line cited from Ibn al-Aʿrābī.
rows.anchor: الميثاق: العهد المؤكد باليمين مفعال من الوثاقة والمعاهدة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb يقطعون has several lexical uses: severing kin, cutting a rope, crossing a river, migrating birds, dwindling water, and breathlessness.
rows.anchor: القطع معروف، والمصدر في الرحم القطيعة يقال: قطع رحمه قطيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is the object of يقطعون; أن can substitute for ما or its pronoun in به, preferably the pronoun, and may also express aversion to connection.
rows.anchor: «ما» في موضع نصب ب «يقطعون». و «أن» إن شئت كانت بدلا من «ما» وإن شئت من الهاء في «به»

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: One view says what must be joined is kinship ties.
rows.anchor: واختلف ما الشيء الذي أمر بوصله؟ فقيل: صلة الأرحام.

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Another view says they sever profession from practice by speaking without acting.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمر أن يوصل القول بالعمل فقطعوا بينهما بأن قالوا ولم يعملوا.

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Another view says they affirm some prophets but reject others, breaking the command to believe in all of them.
rows.anchor: أمرأن يوصل التصديق بجيمع أنبيائه، فقطعوه بتصديق بعضهم وتكذيب بعضهم.

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The command is general: it includes God's religion, worship, laws, and limits, with kinship one part of what must be joined.
rows.anchor: فهي عامة في كل ما أمر الله تعالى به أن يوصل. هذا قول الجمهور والرحم جزء من هذا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فساد on earth means worshipping other than God and acting unjustly according to desires, the fullest form of corruption.
rows.anchor: أي يعبدون غير الله تعالى ويجورون في الأفعال، إذ هي بحسب شهواتهم وهذا غاية الفساد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In أولئك هم الخاسرون, هم may be redundant or may begin a second nominal clause whose predicate completes the first.
rows.anchor: و «هم» زائدة ويجوز أن تكون «هم» ابتداء ثان، «الخاسرون» خبره،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A loser is one who diminishes his own share of success; خسْران means loss, as illustrated by Jarir's verse about lost share and honor.
rows.anchor: والخاسر: الذي نقص نفسه حظها من الفلاح والفوز. والخسران: النقصان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari gives خسار, خسارة, and خيسرى senses of misguidance and destruction; the doomed lose themselves and family on Judgment Day and are denied Paradise.
rows.anchor: والخسار والخسارة والخيسرى: الضلال والهلاك. فقيل للهالك: خاسر لأنه خسر نفسه وأهله يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that every lawful covenant a person undertakes must be honored, whether made with a Muslim or another person.
rows.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على أن الوفاء بالعهد والتزامه وكل عهد جائز ألزمه المرء نفسه فلا يحل له نقضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also commands that a feared betrayal be openly repudiated to the other party, thereby forbidding treachery rather than secret breach.
rows.anchor:
وقد قال لنبيه عليه السلام:
وإما تخافن من قوم خيانة فانبذ إليهم على سوآء
[الأنفال: 58] فنهاه عن الغدر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim advised his sons to follow the religious community; al-Qurṭubī prefers this over identifying it with the nearer phrase أسلمت لرب العالمين, which would mean to say we have submitted.
rows.anchor: أي بالملة وقيل: بالكلمة التي هي قوله: { أسلمت لرب العالمين } وهو أصوب لأنه أقرب مذكور،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وصى and أوصى are synonymous dialect forms used by Quraysh and others, and both are recited.
rows.anchor: ووصى وأوصى لغتان لقريش وغيرهم بمعنى مثل كرمنا وأكرمنا وقرىء بهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The codex of ʿAbd Allāh has وصى; the ʿUthmānic codex and the readings of Medina and Syria have أوصى, while the remaining readers have وصى, which carries an intensive sense.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله «ووصى»، وفي مصحف عثمان «وأوصى» وهي قراءة أهل المدينة والشام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ويعقوب may be coordinated with Ibrahim as another adviser, or treated as a new clause in which Jacob later advises his own sons.
rows.anchor: رفع بفعله، «ويعقوب» عطف عليه وقيل: هو مقطوع مستأنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael was Hajar's eldest son, whom Ibrahim took to Mecca as an infant; reports give ages of two or fourteen, but al-Qurṭubī says infancy is correct.
rows.anchor: وبنو إبراهيم: إسماعيل، وأمه هاجر القبطية، وهو أكبر ولده نقله إبراهيم إلى مكة وهو رضيع.

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Reports differ on Ishmael's age when brought to Mecca: two years or fourteen years.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان له سنتان وقيل: كان له أربع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael was born fourteen years before Isaac, died at 137 or, in another report, 130, and was 89 when Ibrahim died.
rows.anchor: وولد قبل أخيه إسحق بأربع عشرة سنة، ومات وله مائة وسبع وثلاثون سنة. وقيل: مائة وثلاثون.

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Some identify Ishmael as the son offered for sacrifice; al-Qurṭubī prefers Isaac as the more correct view, to be discussed in al-Ṣāffāt.
rows.anchor: وهو الذبيح في قول. وإسحق أمه سارة، وهو الذبيح في قول آخر، وهو الأصح،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isaac's descendants include Romans, Greeks, Armenians, and Israelites; Isaac lived 180 years and was buried with Ibrahim in the Holy Land.
rows.anchor: ومن ولده الروم واليونان والأرمن ومن يجري مجراهم وبنو إسرائيل. وعاش إسحق مائة وثمانين سنة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Sarah's death Ibrahim married Qantura, daughter of Yaqtan the Canaanite, and had Midian, Midan, Nahshan, Zamran, Nashiq, and Shuyukh; his death preceded the Prophet's birth by about 2,600 years, while Jewish chronology subtracts about 400.
rows.anchor: ثم لما توفيت سارة تزوج إبراهيم عليه السلام قنطورا بنت يقطن الكنعانية، فولدت له مدين ومداين ونهشان وزمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's children will be named in Sūrat Yūsuf.
rows.anchor: وسيأتي ذكر أولاد يعقوب في سورة «يوسف»

rows.speaker: عمرو بن فائد الأسواري وإسماعيل بن عبد الله المكي
rows.claim: They read ويعقوب in the accusative, coordinating him with إبراهيم's sons and making Jacob someone Ibrahim advised.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمرو بن فائد الأسواري وإسماعيل بن عبد الله المكي: «ويعقوب» بالنصب عطفا على «بنيه»

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: He considers the accusative reading remote: Jacob was not among Ibrahim's sons or alive to hear the advice, though Jacob also advised his own children.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري: وقرىء «يعقوب» بالنصب عطفا على «بنيه» وهو بعيد لأن يعقوب لم يكن فيما بين أولاد إبراهيم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He reports that Jacob, seeing Egyptians worship idols, fire, and cattle, gathered his sons out of concern and asked what they would worship after him.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: لما دخل يعقوب إلى مصر رآهم يعبدون الأوثان والنيران والبقر،

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: A folk etymology says Jacob was named for grasping his twin Esau's heel at birth; al-Qurṭubī doubts it because the name is foreign, despite coinciding with an Arabic bird name.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إنما سمي يعقوب لأنه كان هو والعيص توأمين، فخرج من بطن أمه آخذا بعقب أخيه العيص.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob lived 147 years, died in Egypt, and asked to be buried beside Isaac in the Holy Land; Joseph carried him there.
rows.anchor: عاش عليه السلام مائة وسبعا وأربعين سنة ومات بمصر، وأوصى أن يحمل إلى الأرض المقدسة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يا بني means أن يا بني; Ubayy, Ibn Masʿūd, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read the phrase with أن.
rows.anchor: معناه أن يا بني وكذلك هو في قراءة أبي وابن مسعود والضحاك.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He says أن is omitted because a testament functions like speech; speech-related clauses allow it either to appear or be omitted, and he rejects the grammarians' explanation that it was intended but elided.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: ألغيت أن لأن التوصية كالقول، وكل كلام يرجع إلى القول جاز فيه دخول أن

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: He parses يا بني as a vocative with the possessive yāʾ opened to avoid two adjoining quiescent letters, like بمصرخي.
rows.anchor: النحاس: «يا بني» نداء مضاف، وهذه ياء النفس لا يجوز هنا إلا فتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن is read with kasra because وصى and قال function as speech, or alternatively because an implicit speech verb is understood.
rows.anchor: إن الله } كسرت «إن» لأن أوصى وقال واحد. وقيل: على إضمار القول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اصطفى means chose; the rajaz line illustrates the form.
rows.anchor:
اصطفى } اختار. قال الراجز:
يا بن ملوك ورثوا الأملاكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الدين means Islam, and the definite article refers to the religion already known to them.
rows.anchor: لكم الدين } أي الإسلام والألف واللام في «الدين» للعهد لأنهم قد كانوا عرفوه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise command means remain committed to Islam and never leave it until death; its brevity both conveys the command and warns of death, whose time is unknown.
rows.anchor: الزموا الإسلام ودوموا عليه ولا تفارقوه حتى تموتوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order is a prohibition with emphatic nūn; تموتن is jussive and loses its waw because two quiescent letters meet.
rows.anchor: «لا» نهي «تموتن» في موضع جزم بالنهي، أكد بالنون الثقيلة، وحذفت الواو لالتقاء الساكنين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلا وأنتم مسلمون is a subject-predicate clause functioning circumstantially; مسلمون is also explained as having good hope in God, sincere, surrendered, or believing.
rows.anchor: «إلا وأنتم مسلمون» ابتداء وخبر في موضع الحال أي محسنون بربكم الظن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address challenges Jews and Christians who attribute to Ibrahim a religion he did not prescribe: they did not witness Jacob's testament and are falsely claiming knowledge.
rows.anchor: والخطاب لليهود والنصارى الذين ينسبون إلى إبراهيم ما لم يوص به بنيه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أم means بل, shifting to a reproachful question about whether their ancestors witnessed Jacob; شهداء is the predicate of كان and is a plural of شاهد.
rows.anchor: و «أم» بمعنى بل أي بل أشهد أسلافكم يعقوب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first إذ is governed by the sense of witnessing, and the second is appositional to it.
rows.anchor: والعامل في «إذ» الأولى معنى الشهادة، و «إذ» الثانية بدل من الأولى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's being overtaken by death means its preliminaries and causes, since a person actually at death could not speak.
rows.anchor: ومعنى «حضر يعقوب الموت» أي مقدماته وأسبابه وإلا فلو حضر الموت لما أمكن أن يقول شيئا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording asks what they worship rather than whom to test what they would say; it also fits the customary inanimate objects worshipped besides God.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن المعبود ب «ما»: ولم يقل من لأنه أراد أن يختبرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من بعدي means after my death.
rows.anchor: ومعنى «من بعدي» أي من بعد موتي.

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: An account says Jacob, when given the prophets' choice, chose death but requested time to advise his family; his sons answered faithfully and affirmed knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: وحكي أن يعقوب حين خير كما تخير الأنبياء اختار الموت وقال: أمهلوني حتى أوصي بني وأهلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim, Ismail, and Isaac are genitive appositions and remain indeclinable because they are foreign names; al-Kisāʾī permits Arabic derivations that would make Isaac or Jacob declinable.
rows.anchor: «إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحق» في موضع خفض على البدل، ولم تنصرف لأنها أعجمية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls both the uncle and grandfather a father, and names the grandfather before Ismail, the uncle, because Ismail was older than Isaac.
rows.anchor: وسمى الله كل واحد من العم والجد أبا، وبدأ بذكر الجد ثم إسماعيل العم لأنه أكبر من إسحق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلها is an indefinite apposition to إلهك, repeated to express God's oneness; it may instead be a circumstantial accusative, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers a good account of the intended affirmation.
rows.anchor: و «إلها» بدل من «إلهك» بدل النكرة من المعرفة وكرره لفائدة الصفة بالوحدانية.

rows.speaker: الحسن ويحيى بن يعمر والجحدري وأبو رجاء العطاردي
rows.claim: They read وإله أبيك; one explanation has the singular refer only to Ibrahim and avoids calling Ismail a father, though al-Naḥḥās says Arabs do call an uncle a father.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ويحيى بن يعمر والجحدري وأبو رجاء العطاردي «وإله أبيك»

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: A second explanation parses أبيك as a sound plural of أب, supported by poetic examples.
rows.anchor: على مذهب سيبويه أن يكون «أبيك» جمع سلامة حكى سيبويه أب وأبون وأبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ونحن له مسلمون is a nominal clause or a circumstantial clause governed by نعبد.
rows.anchor: ونحن له مسلمون } ابتداء وخبر ويحتمل أن يكون في موضع الحال، والعامل «نعبد».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purchase metaphor extends from their choosing misguidance over guidance to choosing its consequent punishment over forgiveness, since punishment follows misguidance and forgiveness follows the guidance they cast aside.
rows.anchor: ولما كان العذاب تابعا للضلالة وكانت المغفرة تابعة للهدى الذي اطرحوه دخلا في تجوز الشراء.

rows.speaker: الجمهور ومنهم الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: They take ما as an exclamation directed at people: marvel at how long the condemned endure in Hell; the construction resembles other Qur'anic exclamations.
rows.anchor: مذهب الجمهور منهم الحسن ومجاهد أن «ما» معناه التعجب وهو مردود إلى المخلوقين،

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن جبير والربيع
rows.claim: They say the people have no patience for Hell; rather, the phrase means how brazen they are toward it, a known Yemeni expression.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة وابن جبير والربيع: ما لهم والله عليها من صبر، ولكن ما أجرأهم على النار!

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: In al-Farrāʾ's report from him, a Yemeni judge used ما أصبرك على الله to mean how bold you are toward God.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: أخبرني الكسائي قال: أخبرني قاضي اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the boldness reading, their conduct is called courageous because it leads to Hell.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: ما أشجعهم على النار إذ يعملون عملا يؤدي إليها.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He says ما means what keeps them in the Fire, as in asking what keeps someone in prison.
rows.anchor: وحكى الزجاج أن المعنى ما أبقاهم على النار من قولهم: ما أصبر فلانا على الحبس!

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Another reading makes their lack of distress at Hell into patience, meaning how little they grieve over it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى فما أقل جزعهم من النار فجعل قلة الجزع صبرا.

rows.speaker: الكسائي وقطرب
rows.claim: They understand the phrase as describing how persistent the condemned are in the deeds of Hell's people.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي وقطرب: أي ما أدومهم على عمل أهل النار.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي وعطاء وأبو عبيدة معمر بن المثنى
rows.claim: They read ما as an interrogative rebuke: what has made them persist in deeds of Hell's people?
rows.anchor: وقيل: «ما» استفهام معناه التوبيخ قاله ابن عباس والسدي وعطاء وأبو عبيدة معمر بن المثنى،

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: A further explanation treats the wording as belittling and dismissing them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا على وجه الاستهانة بهم والاستخفاف بأمرهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: برزوا means they came into the open, broad plain land.
rows.anchor: برزوا } صاروا في البراز وهو الأفيح من الأرض المتسع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jalut was king and commander of the Amalekites, said to cast a one-mile shadow; the Berbers are said to descend from him, and one report numbers his force at 300,000 cavalry.
rows.anchor: وكان جالوت أمير العمالقة وملكهم ظله ميل. ويقال:، إن البربر من نسله،

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He gives Jalut's force as 90,000 rather than the other report's 300,000.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: في تسعين ألفا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the enemy's great numbers, the believers supplicated, as in the account of the many prophets' followers who prayed for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ولما رأى المؤمنون كثرة عدوهم تضرعوا إلى ربهم وهذا كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet would say in battle that by God he attacks and maneuvers, and would seek protection from the enemy's evil while asking God to meet them at their throats.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا لقي العدو يقول في القتال: «اللهم بك أصول وأجول»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Badr he prayed until his cloak fell from his shoulders, urgently asking God to fulfill His promise; the account is discussed under Āl ʿImrān.
rows.anchor: ودعا يوم بدر حتى سقط رداؤه عن منكبيه يستنجز الله وعده

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: He says he was told that the debt verse was the latest Quranic revelation at the Throne.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب: بلغني أن أحدث القرآن بالعرش آية الدين.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says the verse was revealed specifically about salam, prompted by the people of Medina, but by consensus it covers all deferred debt transactions.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هذه الآية نزلت في السلم خاصة. معناه أن سلم أهل المدينة كان سبب الآية،

rows.speaker: ابن خويزمنداد
rows.claim: He says the verse contains thirty legal rulings.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن خويزمنداد: إنها تضمنت ثلاثين حكما.

rows.speaker: بعض علمائنا
rows.claim: Some Maliki scholars infer that loans may be deferred because the verse does not distinguish loans from other debt contracts; the Shafiʿis reply that it only orders documentation of an already deferred debt and that term rules come from other evidence.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل بها بعض علمائنا على جواز التأجيل في القروض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بدين is emphatic; a debt is a transaction with one present countervalue and another deferred in liability, since Arabs call what is present عين and what is absent دين.
rows.anchor:
بدين } تأكيد، مثل قوله
ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording إلى أجل مسمى states the required known, fixed term; two poetic lines use دين for a deferred rather than immediate obligation.
rows.anchor: وقد بين الله تعالى هذا المعنى بقوله الحق { إلى أجل مسمى

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: He says إلى أجل مسمى proves salam with an unknown term is invalid, as also shown by Prophetic practice.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: دل قول الله «إلى أجل مسمى» على أن السلم إلى الأجل المجهول غير جائز،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He transmits the Prophet's rule for advance purchase of dates: specify measure, weight, and term; al-Qurṭubī says Bukhari, Muslim, and others recorded it.
rows.anchor: ثبت أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قدم المدينة وهم يستلفون في الثمار السنتين والثلاث

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: He says pre-Islamic buyers sold camel meat until the offspring of an offspring was born; the Prophet forbade this indeterminate term.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: كان أهل الجاهلية يتبايعون لحم الجزور إلى حبل الحبلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree valid salam specifies described, commonly available food, measure, term, payment in known currency before the parties separate, and delivery place; he knows no scholar who invalidates such a contract.
rows.anchor: وأجمع كل من يحفظ عنه من أهل العلم على أن السلم الجائز أن يسلم الرجل إلى صاحبه في طعام معلوم موصوف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maliki scholars permit tying salam to harvest, fruit-picking, Nowruz, or Mihrajan because these mark known times.
rows.anchor: وقال علماؤنا: إن السلم إلى الحصاد والجذاذ والنيروز والمهرجان جائز إذ ذاك يختص بوقت وزمن معلوم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salam is a sale of a specified, described commodity in liability for present capital or its equivalent, due at a known term.
rows.anchor: هو بيع معلوم في الذمة محصور بالصفة بعين حاضرة أو ما هو في حكمها إلى أجل معلوم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Requiring liability excludes unknown goods and specified individual orchards whose fruit may fail; full description excludes unspecified kinds or qualities of dates, cloth, or fish.
rows.anchor: ومن السلم في الأعيان المعينة مثل الذي كانوا يستلفون في المدينة حين قدم عليهم النبي عليه السلام فإنهم كانوا يستلفون في ثمار نخيل بأعيانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Present capital excludes debt-for-debt; treating it as present permits a two- or three-day delay in paying salam capital, which Malik allows, while al-Shafiʿi and Kufans forbid any delay after contract and separation by analogy with currency exchange.
rows.anchor: تحرر من اليومين والثلاثة التي يجوز تأخير رأس مال السلم إليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī distinguishes salam from currency exchange: exchange has many strict conditions, while salam more closely resembles ordinary transactions and tolerates more flexibility.
rows.anchor: فإن الصرف بابه ضيق كثرت فيه الشروط بخلاف السلم فإن شوائب المعاملات عليه أكثر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A known term excludes spot salam, which is impermissible on the commonly held view, and excludes the pre-Islamic unknown terms.
rows.anchor: وقولهم «إلى أجل معلوم» تحرز من السلم الحال فإنه لا يجوز على المشهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salam and salaf refer to the same transaction, but salam is its specific name because salaf can also mean a loan; salam is a unanimously permitted sale excepted from the ban on selling what one does not possess.
rows.anchor: السلم والسلف عبارتان عن معنى واحد وقد جاءا في الحديث غير أن الاسم الخاص بهذا الباب «السلم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salam is licensed to meet mutual needs: the buyer needs the harvest and the grower needs money before it ripens; it is a sale for the needy, and an immediate sale would defeat that purpose.
rows.anchor: وأرخص في السلم لأن السلم لما كان بيع معلوم في الذمة كان بيع غائب تدعو إليه ضرورة كل واحد من المتبايعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The agreed conditions are six for the goods—liability, description, measurement, deferral, known term, and availability at maturity—and three for capital—known kind, specified measure, and cash payment, with cash status disputed.
rows.anchor: في شروط السلم المتفق عليها والمختلف فيها وهي تسعة: ستة في المسلم فيه، وثلاثة في رأس مال السلم.

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: He says the first requirement, liability, is self-evident because salam is a debt transaction sought for benefit and accommodation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وأما الشرط الأول وهو أن يكون في الذمة فلا إشكال

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: He alone allows salam in a designated item under two conditions: it comes from a secure village, and collection has begun, as with milk from a sheep or ripe fruit from a palm.
rows.anchor: بيد أن مالكا قال: لا يجوز السلم في المعين إلا بشرطين:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He accepts Malik's exceptions: a secure location makes non-delivery unlikely enough to tolerate slight uncertainty, and daily collection of milk or dates meets a recurring need when buyers lack cash or prices fluctuate and sellers need money.
rows.anchor: وهاتان المسألتان صحيحتان في الدليل لأن التعيين امتنع في السلم مخافة المزابنة والغرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophetic wording إلى أجل معلوم settles the requirement for a known term; al-Qurṭubī allows one to three days when prices differ between towns, but not within one town where the price is stable.
rows.anchor: يغني عن قول كل قائل. قلت الذي أجازه علماؤنا من السلم الحال ما تختلف فيه البلدان من الأسعار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is consensus that the term must be known; Malik alone also accepts harvest or fruit-picking as a sufficiently known deadline, discussed under the verse about lunar phases.
rows.anchor: وأما الشرط الخامس وهو أن يكون الأجل معلوما فلا خلاف فيه بين الأمة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is consensus that the goods must exist at maturity; if they fail to exist then through God's decree, the contract is dissolved according to all scholars.
rows.anchor: وأما الشرط السادس وهو أن يكون موجودا عند المحل فلا خلاف فيه بين الأمة أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seller need not own the goods throughout the contract; reports from Ibn Abi Awfa and Ibn Abza say the Companions did not ask Syrian sellers whether they farmed the grain or oil they promised.
rows.anchor: ليس من شرط السلم أن يكون المسلم إليه مالكا للمسلم فيه خلافا لبعض السلف،

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: He requires the goods to exist continuously from contract through maturity, fearing that the promised goods may be unavailable when demanded; other jurists require existence only at maturity.
rows.anchor: وشرط أبو حنيفة وجود المسلم فيه من حين العقد إلى حين الأجل،

rows.speaker: الكوفيون والثوري
rows.claim: They require the delivery location for goods involving transport and invalidate salam if it is omitted; al-Awzāʿī calls omission disliked.
rows.anchor: وشرط الكوفيون والثوري أن يذكر موضع القبض فيما له حمل ومؤنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the place is unstated, the contract remains valid and delivery defaults to the contract location, as held by Ahmad, Ishaq, and hadith scholars; the Ibn ʿAbbās report omits the place, although it specifies measure, weight, and term.
rows.anchor: وعندنا لو سكتوا عنه لم يفسد العقد، ويتعين موضع القبض

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report through ʿAṭiyya says the Prophet forbade redirecting an advance-purchase contract to a different commodity; ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq says the transmitter al-ʿAwfī is not an authority, despite prominent scholars transmitting from him.
rows.anchor: من أسلف في شيء فلا يصرفه إلى غيره

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: If a salam seller cannot deliver at maturity and the buyer releases him, the buyer may take only the original currency or exact capital; exchanging it for another good before receipt would sell food before possession, which the Prophet forbade.
rows.anchor: قال مالك: الأمر عندنا فيمن أسلف في طعام بسعر معلوم إلى أجل مسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فاكتبوه commands recording the debt and its term; some say it also implies witnesses, since writing without witnesses is not legal proof, and it prevents forgetting.
rows.anchor: فاكتبوه } يعني الدين والأجل. ويقال: أمر بالكتابة ولكن المراد الكتابة والإشهاد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says Adam first denied a written gift: God showed him David among his descendants, allowed forty years of Adam's thousand-year life to be added to David's sixty, recorded and witnessed the gift, then produced the document when Adam denied it; David received a hundred years and Adam completed his thousand.
rows.anchor:
عن ابن عباس قال:
" قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قول الله عز وجل { إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to write calls for recording every detail that identifies the debt, preventing disputes and enabling a judge to decide if the parties later disagree.
rows.anchor: إشارة ظاهرة إلى أنه يكتبه بجميع صفته المبينة له المعربة عنه للاختلاف المتوهم بين المتعاملين،

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: He holds that documenting every debt, whether sale or loan, is obligatory to prevent forgetfulness or denial.
rows.anchor: ذهب بعض الناس إلى أن كتب الديون واجب على أربابها، فرض بهذه الآية،

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: He says a lender should write while a seller should obtain witnesses.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: من أدان فليكتب، ومن باع فليشهد.

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: He says people regarded the following clause about mutual trust as abrogating the order to write; Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Zayd, and a report from Abu Saʿid are similar.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: كانوا يرون أن «قوله فإن أمن» ناسخ لأمره بالكتب.

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: He says writing was initially obligatory under these words, then God eased the requirement with the clause permitting trusted transactions.
rows.anchor: وذهب الربيع إلى أن ذلك واجب بهذه الألفاظ، ثم خففه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority treat documentation as recommended protection against lost property and doubt; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this correct because a person may waive a financial claim, so there is no abrogation.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: الأمر بالكتب ندب إلى حفظ الأموال وإزالة الريب،

rows.speaker: عطاء وغيره
rows.claim: They say the writer must write when asked if no other writer is available; al-Shaʿbī gives the same ruling.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء وغيره: واجب على الكاتب أن يكتب وقاله الشعبي، وذلك إذا لم يوجد كاتب سواه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He says the writer must do so when free.
rows.anchor: السدي: واجب مع الفراغ. وحذفت اللام من الأول وأثبتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative lam is omitted before a second-person verb but retained with a third-person verb; the text cites 10:58 and a poetic line to illustrate retention and omission.
rows.anchor: وحذفت اللام من الأول وأثبتت في الثاني لأن الثاني غائب والأول للمخاطب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing with justice means accurately recording the claim without adding or subtracting anything.
rows.anchor: بالعدل } أي بالحق والمعدلة، أي لا يكتب لصاحب الحق أكثر مما قاله ولا أقل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The impartial writer stands between debtor and creditor because each might suspect the other of biased documentation; alternatively, the command reflects that some people can write and some cannot.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال «بينكم» ولم يقل أحدكم لأنه لما كان الذي له الدين يتهم في الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase بالعدل attaches to the act of writing rather than the writer, since a child, slave, or careful layperson could write accurately; appointed notaries must still be upright, knowledgeable, and trusted, as Malik says.
rows.anchor: الباء في قوله تعالى { بالعدل } متعلقة بقوله: «وليكتب» وليست متعلقة ب «كاتب»

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: He says official document writers must be legally knowledgeable, upright, and trustworthy.
rows.anchor: قال مالك رحمه الله تعالى: لا يكتب الوثائق بين الناس إلا عارف بها عدل في نفسه مأمون

rows.speaker: الطبري والربيع
rows.claim: They say the writer is obligated to write when asked.
rows.anchor: فقال الطبري والربيع: واجب على الكاتب إذا أمر أن يكتب.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He makes writing obligatory only where refusal would harm the creditor because no substitute writer is available; otherwise the writer has latitude.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: ذلك واجب عليه في الموضع الذي لا يقدر على كاتب غيره،

rows.speaker: الربيع والضحاك
rows.claim: They say the order to write was abrogated by the prohibition against harming a writer or witness; al-Qurṭubī calls this remote because a universal obligation was never established and paid document-writing is permitted.
rows.anchor: وحكى المهدوي عن الربيع والضحاك أن قوله { يأب } منسوخ بقوله { ولا يضآر كاتب ولا شهيد

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: He says the command is guidance, so the writer need not write before being paid.
rows.anchor: ابن العربي: والصحيح أنه أمر إرشاد فلا يكتب حتى يأخذ حقه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb أبى يأبى is an unusual conjugation, grouped with a few other exceptional patterns.
rows.anchor: وأبى يأبى شاذ، ولم يجىء إلا قلى يقلى وأبى يأبى وغسى يغسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The كاف in كما علمه الله may attach to the command that he write as taught, to the meaning of not refusing because God taught him, or—if the clause ends at أن يكتب—to فليكتب in a new sentence.
rows.anchor: الكاف في «كما» متعلقة بقوله { أن يكتب } المعنى كتبا كما علمه الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who owes the debt is the debtor, and must dictate it aloud so his obligation is known.
rows.anchor: وهو المديون المطلوب يقر على نفسه بلسانه ليعلم ما عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إملال and إملاء are two forms: Hijaz and Banu Asad say أمل, Tamim says أملى; the Quran uses both, including 25:5, and the second lām becomes yāʾ for ease.
rows.anchor: والإملاء والإملال لغتان، أمل وأملى فأمل لغة أهل الحجاز وبنى أسد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor dictates because the testimony follows his admission; he must fear God and not diminish the debt, since بَخْس means reduction, as also in 2:228.
rows.anchor: فأمر الله تعالى الذي عليه الحق بالإملاء لأن الشهادة إنما تكون بسبب إقراره.

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Some say سفيها means a minor, but al-Qurṭubī rejects this because an adult may also be financially foolish.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الناس: أي صغيرا. وهو خطأ فإن السفيه قد يكون كبيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse distinguishes the independent debtor from three who cannot dictate: the fool, the weak-minded, and the person unable to dictate; debts can also arise through inheritance distributions.
rows.anchor: جعل الله الذي عليه الحق أربعة أصناف: مستقل بنفسه يمل، وثلاثة أصناف لا يملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fool has poor financial judgment and cannot manage giving or receiving; the word is likened to a loosely woven cloth, and can also describe crude speech associated with shallow minds.
rows.anchor: فالسفيه المهلهل الرأي في المال الذي لا يحسن الأخذ لنفسه ولا الإعطاء منها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic usage applies سفه to weakness of mind or body, as the cited lines demonstrate for judgment and weakened, swaying spear tops.
rows.anchor: والعرب تطلق السفه على ضعف العقل تارة وعلى ضعف البدن أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some distinguish ḍamma for bodily weakness from fatḥa for weakness of judgment; another view treats both as dialects, but he prefers the distinction.
rows.anchor: وقد قالوا: الضعف بضم الضاد في البدن وبفتحها في الرأي، وقيل: هما لغتان.

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: He reports that a mentally impaired trader's family asked the Prophet to interdict him; the Prophet stopped him from selling, then allowed him to trade only if he said there was no deception. Al-Tirmidhī calls the report sound.
rows.anchor:
روى أبو داود عن أنس بن مالك
" أن رجلا على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يبتاع وفي عقله ضعف

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: His historical record gives a related wording requiring the trader to say there is no deception and granting three nights' option on each purchase.
rows.anchor:
وذكره البخاري في التاريخ وقال فيه:
" إذا بايعت فقل لا خلابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trader was Habban ibn Munqidh, though another account calls Munqidh the grandfather of Yahya and Wasiʿ; he lived 130 years and a battle wound to his head impaired his mind and speech.
rows.anchor: وهذا الرجل هو حبان بن منقذ بن عمرو الأنصاري والد يحيى وواسع ابني حبان:

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Al-Dāraquṭnī transmits that Habban had poor sight and a head wound, so the Prophet gave him three days' option; his impaired speech rendered لا خلابة as لا خذابة.
rows.anchor:
وروى الدارقطني قال:
" كان حبان بن منقذ رجلا ضعيفا ضرير البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلابة means deception, as in the proverb that if one cannot overcome someone, one should trick him.
rows.anchor: الخلابة: الخديعة ومنه قولهم: «إذا لم تغلب فاخلب».

rows.speaker: أحمد وإسحاق
rows.claim: They support interdicting a person who is repeatedly cheated in sales because of inexperience or impaired judgment; other scholars oppose interdiction, and the Maliki school has both views.
rows.anchor: فقال بالحجر عليه أحمد وإسحاق. وقال آخرون: لا يحجر عليه. والقولان في المذهب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers interdiction under this verse and the family's request; the Prophet's concession was specific to Habban because he insisted on trading, while someone ordinarily cheated—especially through mental impairment—should be interdicted.
rows.anchor: والصحيح الأول لهذه الآية، ولقوله في الحديث: يا نبي الله أحجر على فلان.

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق عن محمد بن يحيى بن حبان
rows.claim: The Prophet told Habban to say لا خلابة when selling and gave him three nights to keep or return each purchase; Habban invoked this right even when mocked by sellers, and Companions confirmed his claim. Al-Dāraquṭnī records it; Abu ʿUmar cites al-Bukhari's historical transmission.
rows.anchor: إذا بعت فقل لا خلابة ثم أنت في كل سلعة تبتاعها بالخيار ثلاث ليال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weak debtor is someone impaired in reason or nature and unable to dictate because of stammering, muteness, or inability to express himself; his guardian may be a father or trustee.
rows.anchor: الضعيف هو المدخول العقل الناقص الفطرة العاجز عن الإملاء، إما لعيه أو لخرسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person unable to dictate includes a minor, whose guardian is a trustee or father, and an absent person unable due to illness or another excuse, whose guardian is an agent; a mute could fit either category but fits unable best.
rows.anchor: والذي لا يستطيع أن يمل هو الصغير، ووليه وصيه أو أبوه والغائب عن موضع الإشهاد،

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: He takes وليه to refer to the debt itself, with reports from al-Rabiʿ and Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Qurṭubī rejects this as unsound and says Ibn ʿAbbās's report is not reliable.
rows.anchor: ذهب الطبري إلى أن الضمير في { وليه } عائد على «الحق» وأسند في ذلك عن الربيع، وعن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وليّه correctly refers to the debtor; having the creditor dictate a new liability for a fool would not be lawful, though a sick or mute person may hear a creditor's fair dictation and acknowledge it when complete.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عائد على { الذي عليه الحق سفيها } وهو الصحيح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the debtor is trusted to dictate, a pledgor's sworn account of the debt prevails while the collateral remains; most jurists and Ibn al-Mundhir agree because the creditor claims the excess, in keeping with the rule that the claimant bears proof and the defendant swears.
rows.anchor: لما قال الله تعالى: { فليملل الذي عليه الحق } دل ذلك على أنه مؤتمن فيما يورده ويصدره،

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: He accepts the pledgee's sworn account only up to the collateral's value, treating the pledge and oath as supporting him; al-Qurṭubī says the verse instead favors the debtor, and collateral value need not match the debt.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: القول قول المرتهن فيما بينه وبين قيمة الرهن ولا يصدق على أكثر من ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If وليّه means guardian, the verse implies that a guardian's acknowledgment is valid for the orphan under his care.
rows.anchor: وإذا ثبت أن المراد الولي ففيه دليل على أن إقراره جائز على يتيمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transaction by an interdicted fool without the guardian's permission is invalid by consensus; an unimpaired but foolish person who has not been interdicted is discussed under Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
rows.anchor: وتصرف السفيه المحجور عليه دون إذن وليه فاسد إجماعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking witnesses is recommended, not obligatory, as al-Qurṭubī explains later.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنه ندب على ما يأتي بيانه إن شاء الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God generally requires two witnesses for financial and bodily claims and legal penalties, except adultery; شهيد is an intensive form suggesting repeated testimony and thus justice.
rows.anchor: رتب الله سبحانه الشهادة بحكمته في الحقوق المالية والبدنية والحدود وجعل في كل فن شهيدين إلا في الزنا،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says رجالكم means free men; Shurayh, Uthman al-Batti, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr accept an upright slave's testimony, unlike Malik, Abu Hanifa, al-Shafiʿi, and the majority; al-Qurṭubī prefers the majority, while al-Shaʿbi and al-Nakhaʿi permit slaves' testimony in minor matters.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: المراد الأحرار، واختاره القاضي أبو إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects slave testimony because the address concerns transacting believers, while slaves do not own such assets independently; he also invokes the later restriction on witnesses refusing a summons.
rows.anchor: والصحيح قول الجمهور لأن الله تعالى قال: { يأيها الذين آمنوا إذا تداينتم بدين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He transmits the Prophet's instruction that a witness should testify only to what is as clear as seeing the sun, establishing direct certainty rather than inference.
rows.anchor: مثل ما روي عن ابن عباس قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses must directly know what they attest: probable inference may suffice for ordinary acts such as accepting a gift or recognizing a spouse by voice, but not testimony about another's admission, sale, slander, or seizure.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على اشتراط معاينة الشاهد لما يشهد به، لا من يشهد بالاستدلال الذي يجوز أن يخطىء.

rows.speaker: الشافعي وابن أبي ليلى وأبو يوسف
rows.claim: They accept testimony after blindness when the witness already knew the person before losing sight, analogizing the impairment to absence or death; al-Qurṭubī sees no reason to reject testimony previously borne while sighted and accepts public knowledge for lineage.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال الشافعي وابن أبي ليلى وأبو يوسف: إذا علمه قبل العمى جازت الشهادة بعد العمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some accept a blind person's voice-based testimony as certain, but al-Qurṭubī rejects this because it would imply that a sighted person could likewise rely on sound alone.
rows.anchor: ومن العلماء من قبل شهادة الأعمى فيما طريقه الصوت لأنه رأى الاستدلال بذلك يترقى إلى حد اليقين،

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik permits an established voice-based testimony by a blind person, including on divorce; Ibn Qasim reports him accepting testimony from a man who heard his neighbor divorce through a wall, with several early jurists sharing the view.
rows.anchor: قلت: مذهب مالك في شهادة الأعمى على الصوت جائزة في الطلاق وغيره إذا عرف الصوت.

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: If two male witnesses are not produced, the claimant should bring one man and two women; the male noun is nominative and the women coordinated, with the predicate omitted to mean they take the two men's place.
rows.anchor: المعنى إن لم يأت الطالب برجلين فليأت برجل وامرأتين هذا قول الجمهور.

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Another parsing says the female witnesses may be used only when no men can be found; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this weak because the verse's apparent sense allows one man and two women even when two men are available.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: بل المعنى فإن لم يكن رجلان، أي لم يوجدا فلا يجوز استشهاد المرأتين إلا مع عدم الرجال.

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The one-man-and-two-women arrangement applies to financial matters and requires a man, since financial transactions are common and have multiple safeguards: writing, witnesses, collateral, and guarantees.
rows.anchor: فأجيزت في الأموال خاصة في قول الجمهور، بشرط أن يكون معهما رجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debt-transactions clause does not encompass testimony about a marriage dowry or settlement for intentional homicide, because those testimonies concern marriage rather than debt.
rows.anchor: ولا يتوهم عاقل أن قوله تعالى { إذا تداينتم بدين } يشتمل على دين المهر مع البضع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women may testify alone in matters that no one else can observe, out of necessity.
rows.anchor: وأجاز العلماء شهادتهن منفردات فيما لا يطلع عليه غيرهن للضرورة.

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik permits children's testimony in injuries among children if they have not disagreed or separated; at least two are required, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr also judged by it, which Malik calls established practice.
rows.anchor: فأجازها مالك ما لم يختلفوا ولم يفترقوا.

rows.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: They reject children's testimony because children lack the qualifications of men, approved witnesses, and just adults named elsewhere in scripture.
rows.anchor: ولم يجز الشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه شهادتهم لقوله تعالى { من رجالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because two women replace one man, he reasons by analogy that their testimony can be accompanied by an oath just as one man's testimony can; al-Shafiʿi agrees, while Abu Hanifa and his companions reject the oath as an extra division beyond the text.
rows.anchor: لما جعل الله سبحانه شهادة امرأتين بدل شهادة رجل وجب أن يكون حكمهما حكمه

rows.speaker: الثوري والأوزاعي وعطاء والحكم بن عتيبة وطائفة
rows.claim: They oppose judgment by an oath with a witness; some call that practice abrogated by the Quran, and ʿAṭāʾ alleges ʿAbd al-Malik first ruled that way while al-Ḥakam attributes it to Muʿāwiya.
rows.anchor: وممن قال بهذا القول الثوري والأوزاعي وعطاء والحكم بن عتيبة وطائفة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī calls those accusations mistaken: the verse does not negate the Prophet's ruling by an oath and one witness, and an exclusive reading would also invalidate claims proved when a defendant refuses to swear, contrary to consensus.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله غلط وظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا، وليس من نفى وجهل كمن أثبت وعلم!

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: He argues that when a defendant denies a claim and refuses the oath, the claimant may swear and establish it; because this accepted procedure is absent from the Quran's witness list, its existence proves the list is not exhaustive and supports the oath with one witness.
rows.anchor: قال مالك: فمن الحجة على من قال ذلك القول أن يقال له: أرأيت لو أن رجلا ادعى على رجل مالا
